missing: Measured sustained charging wattage over a real drive (especially in heat, with and without active cooling) for each mount, paired with the car adapter wattage actually needed and current prices — nobody shows checkable throttling or charge-rate numbers.
why: No major reviewer tests MagSafe car mount chargers head-to-head: Macworld answers in part (reviewed Pitaka and ESR picks inside a general MagSafe charger guide), WIRED has a single car entry in a broad gallery, and Tom's Guide covers generic car mounts. The rest is four recycled-template listicles, two affiliate roundups, and four niche sites (Mount Guys, Dash & Drive, izreview, BaniCar, Gadgeteer) that pick with specs but no checkable testing. A focused page with current prices, measured charge rates and a direct pick could get in, but would compete with Macworld's partial coverage.
